notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware backend exists for this simulated R0 package and no hardware run is claimed. The package covers one of the card's five entry symbols: metagym.bandits:Bandits through the registered bandits-v0 environment (arms=50, max_steps=1000); LiftSim, MetaLM, MetaAntEnv and MetaHumanoidEnv are not covered. The action bound action.index 0..49 is derived by the Gymnasium bridge from the fake's Discrete(50) space; the driver declares no own Limit. gym is not installed and package code never imports numpy or the clone, so fake.py is a pure Python standard-library stand-in and was not compared with the upstream environment; the sim backend (gym.make) was not run. Honest differences are recorded in the fidelity gaps, including: the fake installs a placeholder gain table in __init__ because upstream reset() raises until set_task() has run; the fake uses Python's random.Random while upstream draws from numpy's global random generator; and the fake omits the inherited gym.Env helpers (close, render, seed). Bandits draws its task and reward from numpy's global random generator and the class defines no seed method of its own, so the bridge records a supplied seed but the class's own draws are not tied to it; the fidelity determinism kind is therefore statistical, reset is partial. Expected warnings: G6.NO_NATIVE_CALL for cap.world.seed.v1 (the bridge records the next seed and makes no native call; the class defines no seed method of its own) and four G8.NO_UNIT for the bridge-derived integer inputs (ticks, action.index, and seed in both the reset and seed classes). No x-cap ids are used, so there are no catalogue requests. gate.digest is the digest line the last check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run.
